name: Inter-node all-reduce runs at roughly half speed under SR-IOV InfiniBand VF pass-through into VMs, and NCCL needs a hand-written topology XML to even see the fabric
symptom: Two physical A100 SXM4*8 nodes with two HDR InfiniBand cards each, with SR-IOV VF pass-through into a VM per node (host NUMA and PCIe topology mirrored, hugepages and vCPU pinning applied): inter-node all_reduce_perf runs at about 56% of expected. To get NCCL to recognise the topology at all, a topology xml had to be hand-authored and injected with NCCL_TOPO_FILE, listing every PCI busid, link_speed and link_width per NUMA node - the virtualised view is not usable as NCCL's auto-discovery input.
root_cause: Passing an SR-IOV virtual function into a guest gives the guest a different, narrower device identity from the physical NIC, and NCCL's sysfs-based topology discovery does not reconstruct the host's rail layout from that virtual view. Even with a correct hand-written topology file the ~56% figure stands, which points at the virtualised data path itself (VF queue and interrupt overhead, and the host-side SR-IOV switching) rather than at topology misdetection alone. Note the topology XML in the report is also what surfaces the GPU<->NIC pairing that fast designs depend on.
workaround: Author an NCCL_TOPO_FILE for the VM rather than relying on discovery, and pin vCPUs and hugepages as the report does. For inter-node scale-out where all-reduce bandwidth is decision-relevant, pass through the full physical function (PF) rather than a VF, or run on bare metal. Treat any inter-node collective measurement taken under VF pass-through as not comparable to bare-metal numbers.
notes: The virtualisation counterpart to mgpu-mig-slice-nvlink-and-memory-bandwidth-are-shared-not-isolated: MIG's isolation story stops at the GPU, and virtualisation reintroduces shared fabric and a reduced inter-node ceiling underneath it. Also relevant to the existing vllm-arc-b60-no-pcie-p2p-kv-transfer record, which is the same 'no usable P2P transport' problem on a different silicon.
